about.title: Personal Injury Help in Redlands, California
about.longDescription:
Redlands sits where the I-10 threads through the east end of the San Bernardino Valley, and much of daily life here moves along Orange Street, Alabama Street, and Lugonia Avenue. Those same corridors show up most often in public collision records for the city. In 2025, the last complete reporting year, Redlands recorded 477 injury collisions, with 671 people injured and 5 lives lost. Reports tend to rise late on Friday afternoons, roughly 5 to 7 p.m., when commuters, students heading to and from the University of Redlands, and weekend traffic overlap.

A number is just a number until it happens to you. Then it becomes missed shifts, a car you can't drive, and an adjuster asking for a recorded statement. LawProactive exists to make one part of that easier. We are a free service, not a law firm. When you reach out, we listen to what happened and connect you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles cases in San Bernardino County. That attorney works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. You decide whether to move forward; we simply open the door.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Redlands Claim

items.title: Two years to act—sometimes far less
items.desc: Most California injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident. If a city, county, or state agency is involved, a claim may be due in as little as six months.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't shut you out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault. If you share some of the blame, your recovery is reduced by that share, but you are not barred from recovering.

items.title: No fixed cap on pain and suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California does not cap non-economic damages such as pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life.

items.title: Contingency, not hourly billing
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency. You pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: Where do collisions cluster in Redlands?
items.answer: Public collision records for Redlands show the highest counts along I-10, Orange Street, Alabama Street, and Lugonia Avenue. In 2025 the city logged 477 injury collisions and 671 people injured, with reports peaking on Fridays between about 5 and 7 p.m. These are simply where and when the numbers are highest; they reflect traffic volume and are not a judgment about any road.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in California?
items.answer: For most injury claims, the deadline is two years from the date you were hurt. Claims against a government entity, such as a city or Caltrans, can require a written claim within six months. Because these deadlines are strict, it helps to talk with an attorney early.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the crash?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault, but you can still recover for the portion that was not your responsibility. An attorney can review how fault was assigned and whether it was fair.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?

items.answer: Our connection service is free. The attorneys in our network work on a contingency basis, meaning you owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case. The fee terms will be explained to you in writing before you agree to anything.
